content.thinking:
I'm tracing the causal chain here: shoppers' account page requests failed to load, citing G5309 and Gbac1, and now I'm digging into why—tracking down a ZeroDivisionError being raised during request handling.

I need to pinpoint the actual trigger: the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on by an admin, enabling the spend summary code path that caused the error—citing P1, G971b, and Gce95. I'm ruling out deploys as a cause since none occurred around that time, and confirming there was no earlier production change besides this flag flip, using T9 and T10 as evidence. I'm also checking the baseline was healthy before the flag change (G7e5d, Gad41), while noting some pre-existing background ClientDisconnected errors (G46bc) running around 1% that aren't related.

The root cause traces to the function dividing by purchase count, which is empty for shoppers who bought previously but not this month—this rests on F1, and while G5309 confirms the ZeroDivisionError at that line, it doesn't explain why the list was empty, so the chain of reasoning holds and reaches a valid cause.

Looking at the mitigation timeline, the flag was turned off at P2, but Gce95 shows evaluations still returning "on" through 22:15 with errors continuing (G5309)—meaning the revert didn't actually propagate to the service before being flipped back on at T21. I'm also noting that C2's claim about Argus switching off at 22:13:14Z conflicts with the actual record showing P2 at 22:14:25, so I shouldn't cite that candidate. There's also a partial rollout pattern worth checking: G971b shows a 129/71 off/on split at 22:07, but Gce95 reports 200 evaluations all "on" starting at 22:08, suggesting the rollout had fully flipped on by then.

For what stops the harm, since the previous attempt to turn the flag off didn't actually take effect at the service level, the fix has to be the same action—switching monthly-spend-feature off—but this time confirmed by checking the service's own flag-evaluation logs to verify they read "off," that the division-by-zero failures stop, and that the account-page error rate returns to baseline.

For why it didn't help, the record only shows flag evaluations reading "on" through 22:15 after the switch at P2.1, so I should stick to what's documented rather than guess whether this was caching, propagation delay, or an environment mismatch—just note the gap and the lack of visibility beyond 22:15.

For what's still at risk, since the flag ended up back on, account pages for shoppers without purchases this month remain vulnerable to the same failure, and I should state only what's confirmed in the record rather than speculate about anything after that point.

For contributing factors, I'm flagging that no test exercised the monthly-spend path for zero-purchase accounts before the flag went live all at once across the fleet, and since there's no existing remediation item covering this gap, I should propose one requiring flag-gated paths to be tested with the flag enabled, including edge cases.

I'm also noting the flag rolled out to full traffic within a minute with no gradual, error-gated rollout — proposing a staged rollout with automatic halt tied to error rate as the fix. Then I'm considering whether the flag's failure to propagate its off-state at the service level counts as a pre-incident factor or belongs to the response itself.

Evaluations still show "on" within that minute after the switch, though it could just be slow propagation rather than a true failure. I want to phrase it carefully as "the service's flag evaluations still read on in the minute after it was switched off" without over-assuming causation. For the corrective action, I'm weighing something like adding a check that compares the service's evaluated flag state against the provider's state to detect mismatches, rather than jumping straight to a fix that presumes the root cause.

I'm also considering whether to flag that nobody was paged as its own contributing factor, tied back to alert routing configuration predating the incident.

For went_well, I'm noting the Investigator tied errors to the flag switch, Mitigation flipped the flag off then back on when it didn't help, and Code-Fix proposed a draft fix PR without detailing the fix content. For got_lucky, I'm thinking it's mostly empty since the fault only affecting shoppers without recent purchases is really an impact detail already covered elsewhere, not a stroke of luck. Now I'm starting the went_wrong list.

Nobody got paged despite the alert firing, so the incident ended with just a draft PR waiting on a human. More concerning, Mitigation judged the flag revert as refuted and switched it back on even though the service's own logs still showed the flag evaluating as on after the earlier switch-off — meaning it judged an action based on a state change that hadn't actually propagated to the service yet.

The second investigation's findings just repeated the same refuted cause and got a date wrong, so there's nothing new there to act on.

For action items, I'm working through: requiring flag-gated paths to be tested with the flag enabled (covering edge cases like zero-purchase accounts) before production rollout, staged flag rollouts with automatic rollback on error-rate spikes, alerting when the service's evaluated flag state diverges from the provider's setting, and routing high-error-rate alerts to an actual on-call person.

The root cause is clear: the monthly-spend calculation divides total spend by purchase count for the month, which hits zero for shoppers who've bought before but not this month, triggering a division error once the feature flag went live. I'm phrasing the plain-language version carefully, keeping "likely" for the unverified part of the mechanism.

Now I'm building the causal chain: account page requests failed from the start of the incident, citing the relevant evidence tags; the failure traces to a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, avoiding overly specific line numbers; and that code path only ran because the monthly-spend feature was toggled on, with rollout hitting partial then full traffic across the cited time windows.

I'm also ruling out a deploy as the cause — no production changes came back in the deploy history besides the flag flip, and all replicas converged on a single revision, so there's no competing deploy explanation. I'm also noting that before the incident, with the flag off, the pages rendered normally and were error-free, which supports the flag being the trigger.

With the flag on, the monthly-spend calculation divides by the count of this month's purchases, which comes out empty for shoppers who bought previously but not this month — that's the root cause, citing F1. I should assume the logged flag evaluations after the switch-off reflect the actual state used by the service, and that the error spike corresponds to ZeroDivisionError failures rather than the pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors. For mitigation, the fix is to switch the monthly-spend feature off again so the service itself evaluates it as off.

I need to check that the flag evaluation logs confirm "off" and that the ZeroDivisionError failures on the account page actually stop. I should also investigate whether the earlier switch-off reached the service at all, since its evaluations still read "on" a minute afterward — and if it did reach the service, why the failures continued regardless.

action_items.item: Require any code path behind a feature flag to pass tests with the flag on, including accounts with no purchases this month, before the flag can be switched on in production.
Switch feature flags on in production in stages, halting the rollout and switching the flag back off automatically when the service's error rate rises.
Alert when the flag state the service evaluates does not match the flag provider's setting after a flag change.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged a rising account page error rate.
The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. Before the onset the service did not log this error.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. The production change reads returned no deploy, only the flag change, and every replica ran one revision.
The service as it ran with the flag off. Before the flag change, evaluations read off, account pages rendered normally and the account page error rate stayed low.

causal_chain.step: The spend summary path ran because admin switched the feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The service's flag evaluations read on for part of its traffic at {G971b.6} and for every evaluation in the minutes after that.
With the flag on, the function divides by the number of this month's purchases, and that number is zero for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spend feature exposed a calculation on the shop's account page that likely divides by the number of purchases a shopper made this month, so it fails for shoppers who have bought nothing yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production, no check was seen that exercised the code path it enables against accounts with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Such a check would have raised the division by zero before the flag reached shoppers, so the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from part of the service's evaluations to all of them in the minute after it was switched on. No staged rollout and no automatic switch-off on a rise in errors was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that halted on the rise in account page errors would have kept the failures to a small share of shoppers and switched the flag back off without waiting for the alert.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The service's flag evaluations still read monthly-spend-feature as on in the minute after the flag was switched off at the provider. Nothing was seen that would flag a gap between the provider's setting and what the service evaluates.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: If the switch-off had reached the service, or the gap had been flagged, the flag revert could have ended the failures instead of being judged as not helping and put back.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent tied the account page failures to monthly-spend-feature being switched on, from the flag change and the error logs.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature off as a reversible first action.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request, PR #407, for a person to review.

went_wrong: Nobody was paged. The alert fired and the incident ended escalated with a draft fix waiting for a person, but no on-call incident was linked to it.

The flag revert was judged as not helping, and the flag was switched back on, even though the service's own evaluations still read the flag as on in the minute after the switch-off. The revert was never seen to reach the service.

The second investigation offered the same refuted flag cause again, so Argus had nothing new to try. Its account also gave a different time for Argus's switch-off than the flag provider's record shows.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the month's total by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is zero, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: monthly-spend-feature had been switched back on and the division in the spend summary was unchanged, so account page requests from shoppers with no purchases this month could keep failing, and switching the flag on at any later time would fail the same way.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again, and confirm at the service that its flag evaluation log lines read off and that the ZeroDivisionError account page failures stop.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether Argus's switch-off of monthly-spend-feature at {P2.1} reached the service, since its flag evaluations still read on in the minute after it. If it did reach the service, find out why the account page failures went on.
